messages.subject: Role of invalidateLater
parts:
I have a Shiny app for displaying the NYC BikeShare data.

You can view a static, interactive version online here at 

http://ramnathv.github.io/NYCBikeShare/

Alternately, you can run it as a Shiny App

runGitHub('NYCBikeShare', 'ramnathv', ref = 'gh-pages')

My question is connected with what is the best way to make the Shiny App dynamic. Do I need to use invalidateLater so that the data is retrieved after a prespecified time interval, or is that not necessary. Any pointers would be appreciated.

Best,
Ramnath

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Role of invalidateLater
parts:
Very cool.

Yes, you would use invalidateLater to automatically retrieve data periodically. If the data can be shared between all users, then you could do this outside of the server function.

sharedValues <- reactiveValues()
observe({
  invalidateLater(600000)  # ten minutes 
  sharedValues$data <- retrieveData()  # or whatever you do to get the data
})

Elsewhere in your app, just refer to sharedValues$data. (Be sure to check for NULL for the startup case)

This is a less obvious approach than simply doing this:

sharedData <- reactive({
  invalidateLater(60000)
  retrieveData()
})

and referring to sharedData() elsewhere; but the observer/reactiveValues approach is superior because if the value doesn't change from the previous value, then sharedValues$data does not invalidate its dependencies.
